title: Simultaneous Governance Vacuum and Capability Threshold Crossing: A Risk Surface Analysis

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: quantifying detection lag is useful but the model requires many assumptions about capability emergence rates and evaluation frequencies that may not be well-grounded.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Advanced: requires quantitative risk modeling, understanding of scaling laws, and capability emergence dynamics. Beginner CS students would struggle with the modeling assumptions.

narrow_scope.reasoning: No milestone: modeling a 'risk surface' from sparse and uncertain data is open-ended. The inputs (capability emergence rate, evaluation frequency) are themselves research questions.

novelty.reasoning: Research on capability thresholds and governance gaps exists separately but their intersection as a quantitative risk surface is relatively novel. 'The Role of Compute Thresholds for AI Governance' (Institute for Law & AI, 2024) analyzes compute thresholds. 'Focusing AI Governance on Qualitative Capability Leaps' (The Regulatory Review, 2025) addresses capability jumps. GovAI's 'Risk Thresholds for Frontier AI' provides a framework. Evaluation frequency data exists (OpenAI every 2x compute, Anthropic every 4x, DeepMind every 6x). However, no published work explicitly models the joint probability surface of governance vacuum timing AND capability threshold crossing as a quantitative risk analysis. The concept is partially addressed through its component parts but not integrated.
